author: Declaration Desk
title: Ukraine says it hit Russian air base 650 km away; Zelensky mocks Lukashenko's offer to fly him to Moscow
dek: Kyiv's General Staff said five Russian warplanes were put out of action at Savasleyka. Zelensky dismissed a Belarusian offer to escort him to talks with Putin as Washington seeks a new round before Christmas.
body:
Ukraine's armed forces said they struck the Savasleyka air base in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, east of Moscow and roughly 650-700 km from the Ukrainian border, on Tuesday and overnight into Wednesday, knocking three MiG-31 interceptors and two Su-34 fighter-bombers out of action "for some time". Russia did not immediately comment, and the claim could not be independently verified.

The strike came as President Volodymyr Zelensky publicly mocked an offer by Belarus's leader, Alexander Lukashenko, to fly him to Moscow for talks with President Vladimir Putin. "Am I a suitcase or something?" Mr Zelensky said, according to reports. The exchange underlined how far apart the two sides remain on even the venue for talks, as the US administration tries to arrange another round of negotiations before Christmas.

## What happened

Ukraine's General Staff said damage assessment at Savasleyka was continuing. The base is one of the main homes of MiG-31K jets, which carry Russia's Kinzhal air-launched hypersonic missiles, and Ukrainian forces have attacked it several times since August 2024, according to reports.

Ukrainian officials have stepped up long-range strikes in recent weeks. Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said Ukraine had hit 16 Russian ballistic-missile launchers over the past several months, according to reports, and industry sources have said drone attacks cut Russian refinery throughput by 45% since late October. This week Ukrainian drones set fire to two refineries in Samara region, and Kyiv defended strikes on Russian ships off Libya.

Russia has continued its own campaign against Ukraine's energy system and frontline cities. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 153 drones in one overnight attack this week, of which 134 were shot down; Russia's defence ministry said its air defences downed 699 Ukrainian drones over Russia. Casualty and damage figures from both sides are unverified.

## The talks about talks

Mr Lukashenko told the French magazine Le Point that he was willing to accompany Mr Zelensky to Moscow and act as "the guarantor of his security". He argued that Russia, Ukraine and Belarus could end the war faster without European involvement, and said that if Mr Zelensky refused, "let him fight", according to reports.

Speaking to journalists in Berehove in western Ukraine on Tuesday, Mr Zelensky called the offer "not a serious conversation". "We can't meet in Moscow, we can't meet in Kyiv," he said, adding that Mr Lukashenko could instead "take Putin and fly with him to Kyiv", where Ukraine would "guarantee them a safe reception", according to reports. Mr Putin has said he will meet Mr Zelensky only in Moscow; Mr Zelensky has said he is willing to meet on neutral ground.

Kyiv accuses Belarus of letting Russian troops use its territory since the 2022 invasion and of installing relay equipment on the border to guide Russian drones. Belarus has not commented on that accusation in the reports.

Separately, the US administration is seeking to organise a fresh round of peace negotiations before Christmas, according to reports. Mr Zelensky has said US envoys want an agreement "as soon as possible" and that, if talks stall, he will ask the US Congress for further sanctions on Russia.

## Why it matters for India

Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries and ports adds to uncertainty in world fuel markets, which India, as a large buyer of Russian crude, watches closely. India has consistently called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov "exchanged views" in a phone call this week, according to reports; neither side published details of what was discussed on Ukraine.

## What happens next

No date or venue has been set for the next round of talks. Ukraine has said it will stop striking Russian energy targets only if Russia does the same.
